correctness.rationale: For arbitrary d>=2 and positive semiaxes, the Schur complement and projected offset volume give the exact invariant-line chord moment identity. Gaussian polar integration yields the inverse determinant generating series. A convergent positive Laplace integral fixes the final elementary symmetric coefficient since its derivative is strictly negative on x>0; polynomial roots then recover all semiaxes even with multiplicity. Invariance of domain establishes that fewer than d continuous scalar measurements cannot identify the full d-dimensional shape family. Exact rational polynomial cases and independent numerical integrals are reproduced from bundled verify.py.

value.rationale: A natural stereological inverse question is answered by a sharp globally sufficient and dimension-minimal finite set of unlabeled invariant chord moments, with a constructive nonparametric algebraic-plus-monotone recovery for all ellipsoids and repeated axes. This is more than a parameter substitution, case enumeration, or computation of already tabulated moments; key contribution is strict recovery of the last free determinant coefficient.
